upstream.scope: Server-authoritative find-next/find-previous and jump to PID over the published process collection through standard native TextInputs, Buttons and a status Text with standard TEXT_EDIT and ACTIVATE events; search locates rows and never hides, moves or changes one; the current match is held by ItemId and never retargeted automatically; no process action, no protocol, SDK or client change

entries.feature: Search is distinct from filtering: a search query is parsed and matched by the filter's own rules (name and available command text, Unicode case folding, | OR terms, 512-byte and 16-term caps, inert sanitization, monotonic generation) and locates matching rows without hiding, moving or changing any row; matches are counted over the whole server-side collection in published order, and matches the committed filter or the published-row ceiling keep out of the model are counted and stated

Next match and Previous match cycle predictably through the matches in published order and wrap in both directions without changing the row count; a new query selects the first match; no match publishes a visible explanation and disables both buttons so event validation refuses a click
entries.scope: PX-011/search (src/search.rs) Search::step; SEARCH_PREVIOUS and SEARCH_NEXT handlers (src/lib.rs install_search_handlers)

entries.feature: Go to PID resolves a numeric PID (one to ten ASCII digits, read from the field the server kept) to the published row the latest scan confirmed with it and holds that row's ItemId; a missing, filtered-out, beyond-the-ceiling, retained-only or malformed PID is explained instead of selected; when the target stops being shown the search says so and moves to no other process, and a reused PID selects the new live record only through an explicit new search, never by a refresh
entries.scope: PX-011/search (src/search.rs) Search::go_to_pid, Search::observe; refresh (src/refresh.rs) ProcessView unconfirmed set, search effects in apply, set_sort and commit_filter

entries.feature: Search state and controls are bounded: the status is at most 1024 bytes, the PID field keeps at most 32 bytes, the query is bounded by the filter's caps, and the seven new shell nodes are charged a fixed 4096-byte SEARCH_RESERVE_BYTES against the catch-up snapshot; the PX-008 audit admits only the exact SEARCH_INPUT/PID_INPUT TEXT_EDIT and SEARCH_PREVIOUS/SEARCH_NEXT/PID_GO ACTIVATE registrations
